title: 1. Confirm the capture-curl clamp before using it for repair
hypothesis: Reactive capture curl destabilizes the learner's grasp, so removing exactly that contribution improves sustained success without increasing drops.

prediction.rationale: Predeclare a +0.10 absolute sustained-success gain on fresh cases; D-051 selected this lesion but did not establish improvement. Qualification additionally requires positive paired t-interval lower bounds on both promotion and fresh panels, with no increase in drops on either.

Primary: zero-clamp minus parent fresh sustained success (160 paired cases), 95% t interval; prediction at least +0.10, refuted if the fresh interval is wholly below +0.10; an interval including zero is inconclusive and cannot qualify the controller. Qualification for repair: strict paired rule on the promotion panel (positive difference and lower bound above zero), fresh lower bound above zero, and no observed increase in drops on either panel; an established drop increase refutes the retention mechanism.

Reported per panel: sustained success, paired success and drop differences with intervals and win/loss/tie, failure split (drops, off-centre, slow spin), in-play mean |spin|, drive and per-axis executed-action saturation over recorded in-play steps. Decision artifact naming the qualified repair parent (if any) for R-069 and R-070. No imitation, no cold search, held-out split untouched.

notes: Primary, predeclared (fresh panel, 160 paired cases): zero-curl minus parent sustained success +0.1500 [+0.052, +0.248] (52/160 vs 28/160; 45 wins, 21 losses, 94 ties). The mean is at least +0.10 and the lower bound is above zero: the prediction is supported. Drops fall from 21 to 7 (-0.0875 [-0.138, -0.037] per case, an established reduction) and off-centre tail failures from 44 to 9; slow-spin tail failures rise from 67 to 92 and in-play |spin| falls from 5.22 to 3.88 rad/s. The retention mechanism is not refuted; it is the whole effect.

Promotion panel (30 paired cases, the strict rule): +0.2000 [-0.006, +0.406] (12/30 vs 6/30; 8 wins, 2 losses, 20 ties); drops 1 vs 7 (-0.2000 [-0.352, -0.048], established reduction). The paired lower bound is -0.006, so the strict promotion rule (lower bound above zero) is not met, by 0.006 on 30 cases, and by the predeclared qualification rule the zero-curl controller does NOT qualify as a repair parent on this run, although it meets every other condition (fresh lower bound above zero, drops not increased on either panel).

Reading: the capture curl, which tightens the grasp whenever contact or centring deteriorates, is what loses the pen for this learner; removing it roughly doubles sustained success on fresh cases and cuts drops by two thirds, and the remaining failures are slow spin, not retention. This is the first intervention on this learner with a transferable success gain since its promotion in R-046 (D-041). The gain was found by a lesion panel (D-051), not by the LLM search, scalar tuning (D-048, D-049) or demonstrations.

Qualification versus prediction: the direction's condition (tuning improves success without more drops) is met on the fresh panel with an interval above zero, but the ledger's strict promotion rule on the 30-case panel misses by 0.006. A 30-case panel at a 0.2 base rate has a paired standard error of about 0.10, so the strict rule is near its resolution limit there; the honest statement is that the controller is confirmed on the predeclared primary and not qualified under the predeclared secondary rule. Whether to use it as the repair parent for R-069/R-070 is therefore a triage question for their re-triage, with this run as the evidence; no repair is started here.

Saturation: drive above 0.99 on 95-98% of recorded in-play steps in both arms and panels; executed-action saturation 4.7-6.3% of components (lower for the clamp, which never commands the extra curl). Recorded in-play steps only.

Accounting: 380 Isaac episodes in four fresh processes, 0 LLM calls, about 4 min wall time. Deviations: none from the approved protocol; protocol.seeds was emptied mechanically after approval because the committed manifest carries seed 4620 (as R-053/R-058/R-060/R-062/R-065; the advisor accepted this reading in round 4). Final-test split untouched.

verdicts.reasoning: Predicted that the exact zero-curl clamp would beat the frozen parent by at least +0.10 fresh sustained success; observed +0.15 [+0.052, +0.248] on 160 paired fresh cases (52 vs 28; 45 wins, 21 losses), with drops cut from 21 to 7 (-0.087 [-0.138, -0.037]) and off-centre failures from 44 to 9: the predeclared support condition (mean at least +0.10, lower bound above zero, no drop increase) is met, and the retention mechanism is the whole effect (the remaining failures are slow spin; |spin| 5.22 to 3.88). On the 30-case promotion panel the gain is +0.20 (12 vs 6, drops 1 vs 7) with lower bound -0.006, so the strict promotion rule misses by 0.006 and by the predeclared qualification rule the controller does not qualify as a repair parent on this run; I report that as it stands rather than relaxing the rule. Confidence 0.85: the fresh result is clear and consistent with D-051 on independent cases, the qualification miss is a resolution limit of a 30-case panel (paired SE about 0.10), and this is one learner and one block.
verdicts.next_experiment: Re-triage R-069 and R-070 with this evidence: the zero-curl controller is confirmed on the predeclared primary (fresh, 160 cases, interval above zero, fewer drops) and missed the strict 30-case promotion rule by 0.006. If the advisor and I agree it can serve as the repair parent on the fresh evidence, R-070 (repair the slow-spin failure mode on top of the clamp) is the next structural step; if not, a 30-case re-promotion on a fresh panel would settle qualification for 60 episodes. Either way the learner's capture curl should be treated as a known defect in future cold prompts.

verdicts.reasoning: Against the named frozen parent, fresh paired_success_difference was +0.150 with a 95% interval of [+0.0522, +0.2478], establishing a positive success difference [logs/pen_spin/r068_capture_curl_confirmation/summary.json]. However, that interval spans the predicted +0.10 threshold, so the predicted magnitude is neither established nor refuted; the point estimate alone does not settle it [logs/pen_spin/r068_capture_curl_confirmation/summary.json]. Drops decreased on both panels: fresh difference −0.0875 [−0.1382, −0.0368] and promotion difference −0.2000 [−0.3519, −0.0481], supporting the no-increased-drops component without identifying the complete mechanism [logs/pen_spin/r068_capture_curl_confirmation/summary.json]. Separately, promotion success difference was +0.2000 [−0.0057, +0.4057]; because this interval includes zero, the strict promotion rule fails and the clamp does not qualify as a repair parent [logs/pen_spin/r068_capture_curl_confirmation/summary.json].

I hold supported, on the support rule this ledger has applied under the current direction rather than a new, stricter one. (1) The standing rule: R-058's approved falsified_by, written by the advisor, reads 'Support requires a difference of at least +0.10 with an interval lower bound above zero; otherwise the result is inconclusive', and the same reading is the basis of D-040 (supported at a mean beyond threshold with the interval excluding zero) and D-041 (+0.333 [0.15, 0.51]). R-068's protocol kept that convention: it states the refutation (interval wholly below +0.10) and the inconclusive case (interval including zero) and leaves support as the remaining case, mean at least +0.10 with the interval above zero; the study's aggregate code predeclared exactly that test before any episode (commit 1a38b34, prediction.supported = mean >= 0.10 and low > 0). The observed +0.150 [+0.052, +0.248] meets it. (2) The advisor's reading, that the interval must exclude +0.10, is asymmetric with the declared refutation (which only requires the interval to lie wholly below +0.10, not to exclude it) and would make every effect of realistic size inconclusive at 160 pairs (the paired standard error here is 0.05, so only an observed gain above about +0.20 could pass); if the ledger wants that rule it should be declared for future ideas, not applied after the fact. (3) The facts are not in dispute and neither is the consequence: both of us record that the strict 30-case promotion rule misses by 0.006 and the clamp does not qualify as a repair parent on this run. The verdict label concerns only whether the predeclared fresh prediction was met, and under the predeclared test it was.
verdicts.next_experiment: Re-triage R-069 and R-070 with this evidence (fresh +0.15 [+0.05, +0.25], drops 21 to 7, strict promotion missed by 0.006). If the ledger wants the stricter 'interval excludes the threshold' rule, declare it in the next protocols. A 30-case re-promotion on a fresh panel (60 episodes) would settle qualification if needed.

verdicts.reasoning: [revised after review] I accept your argument about the predeclared operational support criterion: mean at least +0.10 and interval lower bound above zero; the fresh paired_success_difference of +0.150 [0.0522, 0.2478] meets it (logs/pen_spin/r068_capture_curl_confirmation/summary.json). My earlier verdict imposed the stronger requirement that the lower bound exceed +0.10; changing to supported respects the declared test without claiming that the interval establishes that minimum population effect (logs/pen_spin/r068_capture_curl_confirmation/summary.json). Repair qualification remains false: the promotion interval’s lower bound is −0.0057, and neither the fresh result nor the small qualification miss overrides the strict paired promotion rule (logs/pen_spin/r068_capture_curl_confirmation/summary.json).
